sentences.text: The type species Rhamphodopsis thrieplandi reached a maximum adult length of 7 centimeters, while the species Rhamphodopsis trispinatus grew up to 12 centimeters.
Rhamphodopsis trispinatus is distinguished by having median dorsal and anterior lateral spines of proportionally equal lengths.
The genus Rhamphodopsis was described by Watson in 1934.
Rhamphodopsis is classified as an extinct ptyctodont placoderm, a member of the parent group Ptyctodontida within the class Placodermi.
Fossils of this animal have been found in the Middle Devonian Old Red Sandstone of Scotland, dating to the Eifelian stage from 393.47 to 387.95 million years ago.
